versions.short: The bill would require the Secretary of State, working with the agencies that run US foreign aid programs, to report to Congress each year through 2030 on any US-funded food, medicine, vaccines, or medical supplies that were destroyed after being spoiled, contaminated, expired, or reaching the end of their useful life. For each destroyed item, the report would have to explain the efforts made to prevent the waste, the reasons the item could not reach its intended recipients (including any local laws that blocked delivery, donation, or sale), the item's purpose and where its intended beneficiaries were, its purchase and market value, and what it cost to destroy it. The reports would go to the Senate and House committees on foreign relations and appropriations.
